title: Choose the visual world for the Open Room product page
question: The roll assigned The Switchboard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Switchboard
options.lineage: 1950s to 70s cord switchboards: jack fields, cloth patch cords, name lamps, one operator
options.thesis: One operator, many lines. Your voice is the headset; each agent is a named jack, and a cord shows exactly who you reached.
materials: cloth-wrapped cords in the five agent colours
options.viewport: A board the full width of the page, edge to edge, dark bakelite on a deep walnut ground. Five jacks in a row, each with an engraved nameplate and a pixel mascot perched on the panel above it. Bottom left, the operator's jack labelled YOU with a live headset meter. A teal cord runs from YOU into Bit's jack; Bit's lamp is lit and its cord tag reads the spoken line. Headline in engraved caps on the board's top rail. One brass button: Download for Windows.
options.risk: Reads as a museum piece if the cords do not move and the lamps do not answer; the board must be an instrument, not a prop.

raised.raise: One ink, one accent, and the accent holds a third of any screen: the board's dark ground and the cord colours own the page, nothing else is coloured.
Every claim is seamed to its source: each feature carries a small stitched caption naming the app fact it comes from.
Motion is drawn in sequence: cords plug in as one continuous stroke, lamps warm up after, nothing fades in from nowhere.

options.label: The Party Screen
options.lineage: 16-bit RPG party and status screens: five companions, HP bars, a quest log, speech bubbles
options.thesis: Your agents are a party. The page is the party screen: five named companions with status bars, a command menu that is your voice, and a quest log that is the transcript.
options.viewport: A bordered panel fills the width: five party slots across the top, each a pixel portrait, a name and a status bar. Below, a command window reading TALK with a blinking cursor and the line 'hey Bit, run the tests' typing in; Bit's slot lights and a speech bubble pops from its portrait. Headline in the window's title bar. Download as the highlighted menu item.
options.risk: The direction most runs land on for pixel mascots; retro-game chrome can read as a joke unless the type and spacing stay disciplined.

options.label: Mecha Command Wall
options.lineage: nineties mecha-anime crisis walls: phosphor orange and acid green on black, hazard chevrons, seven-segment counters
options.thesis: The agents as readings on a crisis wall: five framed label blocks on leader lines from a central schematic, counters ticking as they work.
options.viewport: Black field, five label blocks at the edges wired to a central schematic of the room, each with a counter and a status bar; the spoken line types across the top rail in spaced caps.
options.case: Developers identify with it instantly and the crew's colours survive on black. Loses on clarity: a crisis wall says emergency, and the product's promise is calm.
options.risk: Sirens and countdowns pull against an app whose point is that you can walk away.

options.label: Depot Destination Blind
options.lineage: bus depot destination blinds: dyed cloth courses stepping under one window, chrome-yellow legends
options.thesis: Each agent is a roll of cloth legends stepping under a window: idle, working, done snap one course at a time, and a fault stops mid-step.
options.viewport: Five blind windows in a row, each showing an agent's current legend; saying a name steps that blind to LISTENING with an overshoot and settle; the headline is cut on a bias panel above.
options.case: Holds product clarity: state as a stepped legend is exactly how an agent's status changes. Loses identification: depot cloth is not a world developers know by heart.
options.risk: Three dyes only leaves no room for five agent colours without breaking the system.

options.label: Film Cutting Bench
options.lineage: a film editor's bench: perforated select rail, punched frames, orange tape flags
options.thesis: Sections strung along a perforated rail as frames, the spot you stopped marked by a tape flag.
options.viewport: A perforated rail across the page with the product's sections as frames on it.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing about talking to agents is a film strip, and the rail would be a costume.
options.kept: One ink, one accent, and the accent holds a third of the screen.

options.label: Memory Quilt
options.lineage: hand-pieced quilts from worn garments with handwritten cloth labels
options.thesis: Every feature a pieced block with its caption stitched to it.
options.viewport: A block grid of unequal patches, each feature a patch with a stitched caption.
options.case: Developers do not identify with domestic textile, and a quilt cannot show a voice reaching an agent.
options.kept: Every caption seamed to its source, a visible stitch from claim to fact.
options.risk: Warm and slow where the product is quick.

options.label: Wildstyle Blackbook
options.lineage: a graffiti writer's sketchbook: interlocking marker letters with arrows and bars
options.thesis: The five names as one interlocking piece, arrows leading from one agent's letters into the next.
options.viewport: The crew's names knitted into one mass of letters with a fast throw-up in the corner.
options.case: Illegible by design, and the product's whole point is that a name is instantly clear.
options.kept: Motion drawn in sequence, one continuous stroke at a time.
options.risk: The name is the map, and this map is unreadable.

options.label: Rain-Night Cityscape
options.lineage: an urban nocturne: blue hour into rain, window grids, transit lines, river reflections
options.thesis: Agents as lit windows in a skyline, transit lines carrying your words across the city.
options.viewport: A skyline band with five lit windows and a train of amber light crossing the river.
options.case: Beautiful and anonymous: a city has no operator, and the crew would shrink to five windows.
options.kept: Synchronised bands that reflow on phones without losing their timing.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What developer-tool landing pages ship, executed impeccably.
materials: product screenshot in a rounded window
canonCard.viewport: Centred headline, grey lead, black pill button, the app window below in a rounded panel with the crew as small avatars in its rail.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Cursor, Conductor and Warp by design.
